text.en: The Pamban Bridge in Rameswaram stands in salty sea air, the worst place for iron. It survives only because engineers keep renewing its protective coating. That is applied chemistry fighting corrosion.

An alloy is a homogeneous mixture of two or more metals, or of metals with non-metals, and it can be thought of as a solid solution with the main metal as solvent.
We make alloys to change appearance, to alter chemical activity, to lower the melting point, to increase hardness and tensile strength and to raise electrical resistance.
Alloys are made by fusing metals together, like brass from zinc and copper, or by compressing finely divided metals.
Brass is Cu and Zn, bronze is Cu and Sn, duralumin is Al with Mg, Mn and Cu, magnalium is Al and Mg, and stainless steel is Fe with C, Ni and Cr.
An amalgam is an alloy of mercury with another metal; silver-tin amalgam is used for dental fillings.
Pig iron has 2.0 to 4.5 percent carbon, steel 0.25 to 2.0 percent and wrought iron below 0.25 percent.
Corrosion is the gradual destruction of a metal by chemical or electrochemical reaction with its environment.
Dry corrosion is a direct chemical attack by gases at high temperature; wet corrosion needs moisture and is electrochemical.
Rust is hydrated ferric oxide, Fe2O3.xH2O, formed when iron meets oxygen and moisture.
Corrosion is prevented by alloying, by galvanization (zinc coating), electroplating, anodizing (used for aluminium) and cathodic protection with a sacrificial metal.

problem.en: A student claims a nail kept in dry air will rust quickly. Do you agree?

text.en: Rusting needs both oxygen and moisture.
In dry air there is no water to carry ions between anode and cathode.
So I do not agree; the nail will not rust quickly unless moisture is present.

why.en: Keeping iron dry or coated prevents rust.

prompt.en: Explain why galvanized iron resists rusting even where the coating is scratched.

requiredIdeas.en: Zinc is more reactive than iron
Zinc acts as the sacrificial anode and corrodes first

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking the zinc only works as a physical barrier

points.en: Alloys improve hardness, strength, appearance and resistance; amalgam contains mercury.
Brass: Cu+Zn; bronze: Cu+Sn; steel: Fe+C; stainless steel adds Ni and Cr.
Rust is Fe2O3.xH2O and needs air and moisture.
Prevent corrosion by alloying, coating, galvanizing, anodizing and sacrificial protection.
